# Primary analysis: thirty minutes

```{r}
#| include: false
source(here::here("chapters", "_setup.R"))
# Fitted once by scripts/03_fit_models.R (R/results.R).
by30 <- results$by30
or30 <- results$or30
or_adj <- results$or_adj
```

The primary question (D-001), analyzed as planned with an unadjusted
logistic regression (D-002).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-30min
#| tbl-cap: "Any sore throat at rest, thirty minutes after arrival in recovery."
knitr::kable(
  transform(by30, proportion = fmt_pct(proportion)),
  col.names = c("Arm", "Patients", "With sore throat", "Proportion")
)
```

Sore throat at thirty minutes was less common with licorice
(`r fmt_pct(by30$proportion[by30$group == "Licorice"])` vs
`r fmt_pct(by30$proportion[by30$group == "Sugar"])`; `r fmt_or(or30)`;
`r fmt_p(or30$p_value)`).

**Sensitivity.** Adjusting for the pre-specified baseline covariates (D-007)
gives `r fmt_or(or_adj)`.
This is a conditional odds ratio, so it is expected to sit somewhat further
from one than the unadjusted estimate even with perfect balance
(non-collapsibility; Chapter 4). The two agree on direction and size, and
the adjusted interval is not a test of the unadjusted one. Preoperative pain
is not adjusted for: only
`r sum(clean$preop_pain == "Yes")` patients had any.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
fit_warnings_note(results, c("Primary (30 min)", "Adjusted sensitivity (30 min)"))
```
